# awrtifact

> Deliberately chunk artifacts into GitHub release assets — the productized aitherkvcache mirror lane.

Big artifacts (model weights, datasets, builds) exceed GitHub's 2 GiB release-asset cap, so mirrors end up as bespoke scripts with hardcoded manifests that go stale — the fleet's orchestrator served a pre-v18 build for days while the v18 file sat in a release the worker did not know.

## Install

```
pip install awrtifact
```

## In Claude Code

- skill: `/awrtifact`

## Use it in 30 seconds

Store one artifact as a versioned GitHub release and fetch it back byte-verified — `awrtifact mirror <URL|FILE> --release TAG`.

## Composes with

- [awdk](https://aitherium.github.io/awdk/) — Build AI agent fleets — 3 lines, any backend, local or cloud.
- [awnode](https://aitherium.github.io/awnode/) — A lightweight local gateway — bridges your apps to the AI backends you chose.
- [aitherkvcache](https://aitherium.github.io/aitherkvcache/) — Near-optimal KV cache quantization for LLM inference — sub-byte compression.
- [awgit](https://aitherium.github.io/awgit/) — Semantic version control on top of git — edit-ops and leases.
- [awseal](https://aitherium.github.io/awseal/) — Sign an artifact so a stranger can verify it.
- [awshare](https://aitherium.github.io/awshare/) — Publish an artifact and fetch it back verified.
- [awrecover](https://aitherium.github.io/awrecover/) — Labelled snapshots with an all-or-nothing restore.
- [awstorage](https://aitherium.github.io/awstorage/) — Every drive on every node, indexed, classified and diffed -- so you can see what you own before you delete it.
